Replay

Cavecrawl with owner motion

4 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Authoring and executionRecovery and acceptanceAction-time context and O1 saves

This is an explicit cooperative motion profile beside the original Kit game and the server-simulated Replay Cavecrawl. It reuses that port's gameplay reducer—the function that applies inputs to world state— along with its scenes and interface. A local pose producer samples the player's locally simulated avatar and carried relic; authenticated, versioned pose samples become values in the authoritative replayable world. Inventory, combat, AI, progression and room authority remain server decisions.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl_owned/play.sh
REPLAY_CAVE_ROLE=host nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl_owned/play.sh
REPLAY_CAVE_ROLE=client nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl_owned/play.sh
REPLAY_CAVE_ROLE=observer nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl_owned/play.sh

The default port is 49585. The native user directory is ReplayCavecrawlOwned; browser profile and Party namespaces also differ from the server-simulated port. Content 0x434156454f574e33 and the latest-observation contract are incompatible with server-motion peers/saves. There is no implicit cross-profile conversion. Both Replay profiles and the original Kit game remain independently runnable.

Authoring and execution#

Edit shared gameplay in examples/replay_cavecrawl/shared/cave/ and shared Godot authoring in examples/replay_cavecrawl/scripts/ and its scenes/resources. The owner_cave package composes that world with ownership/sample metadata. Its step supplies accepted positions to the common reducer instead of integrating movement there. Validation requires both representations to agree.

prepare.py OUTPUT creates a fresh isolated project, binds the common scripts to the owner model, changes defaults, and records source hashes. build.sh OUTPUT also builds/imports it. Existing output projects are refused. For a persistent project to inspect in Godot:

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_cavecrawl_owned/build.sh /absolute/fresh/output

play.sh uses a temporary generated project and removes it on exit; game profiles and saves live in the separate persistent user directory. Edit the shared authored source, rather than the temporary project. Assets retain the common port's original provenance.

Keyboard motion is normalized; scripted walk_to uses the original independent axis stepping. Local poses render immediately and are sampled into controls. The original's manual owner movement is not a rigid-body solver, so this variant does not add one or clip movement to the viewport/rift. Late owner poses can settle after a health/victory update; the producer gates new movement from observed state.

Owner changes, floor transitions, respawn/revive, fresh identities and authority epochs invalidate previous sample scopes. Respawn/revive cuts the scope even when coordinates are unchanged. Checkpoints retain accepted pose/velocity, ownership, revision and sample frontiers; replay consumes those values without invoking the local producer. Scope and finite-value bounds are checked, but a cooperative owner is trusted to supply its own pose. This is not competitive movement validation or deterministic Godot physics.

Recovery and acceptance#

The existing Room path supports this model. A provision/checkpoint service can use REPLAY_ROOM_CONTENT=0x434156454f574e33 and REPLAY_ROOM_CHECKPOINT_MODEL=cavecrawl-owned; see the service configuration. Service state must be separate from deployments of the other content IDs.

Shell
REPLAY_CAVE_OWNER_OUT=/absolute/fresh/tests nix develop --command bash tests/replay_cave_owner/run.sh
CHECKPOINT_GAMES=cavecrawl-owned CHECKPOINT_RESTORE=1 REPLAY_CHECKPOINT_OUT=/absolute/fresh/checkpoints nix develop --command bash tests/replay_room_checkpoint/run.sh

The first native gates cover loot/door play, a faulted host → unowned → guest relic handoff, and planned/crash recovery with either successor or surviving guest carrying the relic. Pure model tests check stale/foreign/recycled samples, exact checkpoint installation, epoch rebinding, inventory retention and life/floor cuts. The existing shared reducer and native solo/network gates remain passing.

Three real Chrome instances now pass planned carried-relic handoff; abrupt host loss passes with the two survivors. Owner epochs/revisions, fresh samples, social state, RTC traffic and profile reload are checked. Browser solo saves pass exact restore after a killed browser, continued actions, stale-writer rejection and corruption preservation in the default isolated namespace.

Shell
REPLAY_CAVE_OWNER_WEB_OUT=/absolute/fresh/browser nix develop --command bash tests/replay_cave_owner/browser_run.sh

See browser evidence and limits. This is a new profile, not full original-game parity. Broader browsers and public network deployment, richer fault/recovery cases, remote presentation and paired gameplay/performance/ergonomics comparisons remain acceptance work.

Action-time context and O1 saves#

O2 attaches the local producer's pose and ownership scope to range interactions and throws. The reliable action can be judged before its movement observation, or after a newer observation, without overwriting the avatar's accepted current pose. Take/door/pickup/carry/revive use the issued origin; thrown rocks clamp that origin to within 64 pixels of the accepted avatar position, matching the original rule. Current actor eligibility and target state still apply. Commands entered while a restored producer scope is not ready are held in a bounded 16-entry local FIFO; their origin is captured when submission becomes possible. Leave discards these unsubmitted intents. Respawn, ownership changes and authority epochs retire old contexts. This is a scoped owner claim, not a verified historical simulation pose or competitive anti-cheat.

The lower-level action also supports Accepted_Pose for server-authored commands and O1 compatibility. Ordinary UI actions use Owner_Pose. Action IDs retain the runner's existing ordering and deduplication; contexts do not consume or rewind pose-stream sequences. A preserved pending context from a previous authority epoch is refused normally; a fresh command needs the newly observed scope.

Convert an O1 or O2 native save explicitly to a new destination:

Shell
nix develop --command odin build examples/replay_cavecrawl_owned/tools/upgrade_save \
  -collection:godot=. -out:/tmp/upgrade-owned-cave
/tmp/upgrade-owned-cave /path/to/owner1.replay /path/to/owner3.replay

World, ownership, controls, membership and action frontiers remain unchanged. Pending O1 commands retain accepted-pose semantics; the converter does not invent an issue-time origin. Existing destinations/corrupt files are preserved, and coordinated archives require an application-owned upgrade. The converter does not rewrite browser IndexedDB records. Older browser archives remain protected by strict content checks; interactive cross-version browser import is still pending.

O3 adds the common generation-bound dweller impacts. O2 saves convert with exact world/action preservation; explicit O2 recording verification retains the old event sequence.
